assumptions: Synthetic handler_effect transcribed from rpcd-mod-file rpc_file_exec; C, not ucode

uhttpd uh_ubus_allowed requires session.access scope=ubus object=file function=exec (uhttpd omits scope). rpcd-mod-file then requires session.access scope=file of the canonicalized executable or, on miss, of the cmdline. A ubus file.exec grant is not authorization to run an arbitrary command.

rpc_file_exec_run checks the executable file ACL first, then the cmdline. That is the reverse of cgi-io main_exec. Inventoried luci-ssl ACLs grant the cmdline /sbin/sysupgrade --list-backup, not the bare executable, so extra tokens are PERMISSION_DENIED, not authorization_violation and not a PoC.
This oracle does not fork execv or run the command body.
shellquote and basename are not sanitizers. rpc_canonicalize_path is a textual path normalizer, not a taint sanitizer.
This command is not a luci object method. Do not invent a luci object grant. Callers at luci b2e0be4b use fs.exec → ubus file.exec. cgi-backup / cgi-download stay on their cgi-io grants.
rpc_file_exec_run returns PERMISSION_DENIED when both SID and env are present. Inventoried callers do not pass env.
The luci-mod-system-flash fixture is already list read for cgi-backup and cgi-download. This slice reuses that session; it does not invent a write flash login.
